advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure MCP tools that delegate to public library ops do not double-compose the shadow snapshot (compose once per logical operation).
evidence: _mcp_reads.py: `_shadow("mcp.read.bridge_fsck")` then `return BridgeFsckOut.model_validate(rebar.bridge_fsck())`
_lib_ops.py bridge_fsck: `_shadow(repo_root, "lib.bridge_fsck")` inside the same delegated call
Ticket a377 outcome: 'compose ONE OperationSnapshot per operation'; MCP write bridge_projects_set/remove and read bridge_fsck/bridge_run/etc. all delegate to _lib_ops functions that also shadow
advisory.finding: MCP tools compose the shadow snapshot and then delegate to a public library op that composes it again, so a single MCP operation composes the snapshot twice — contradicting the ticket's 'one immutable snapshot per operation' contract and doubling the (non-trivial) config resolution work on every such call.
scenarios: Any MCP tool that delegates to a public library op (bridge_fsck, bridge_projects_set/remove, bridge_run, get_workflow_status/result, etc.)

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Compose the CLI shadow snapshot with the subcommand's resolved --root so the diagnostic matches the operation's actual root.
evidence: `emit_shadow_snapshot(surface="cli")` passes neither repo_root nor cli_overrides

The `-c` overrides are picked up via the module-global _CLI_OVERRIDES fallback in resolve_with_sources (config.py:648), but `--root` is a per-subcommand flag parsed later in dispatch and is never forwarded to the shadow
test_surfaces_compose_equivalent_snapshot passes an explicit repo_root to compose_operation_snapshot rather than exercising the CLI's own emit_shadow_snapshot root selection
advisory.finding: The CLI shadow is composed with no explicit repo_root (emit_shadow_snapshot(surface="cli")), so when a subcommand supplies --root the shadow resolves the ambient root (REBAR_ROOT/git/cwd) instead of the command's actual --root, making the logged root/fingerprint diverge from the real operation.
scenarios: `rebar <cmd> --root /some/other/repo` where the ambient cwd/REBAR_ROOT differs from --root

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drive the MCP and reconciler surfaces through their real entry points (or a spy on emit_shadow_snapshot capturing the repo_root/cli_overrides they pass) instead of re-calling compose_operation_snapshot with identical args.
evidence: py_snap = compose_operation_snapshot(repo_root=str(p), cli_overrides=overrides)
mcp_snap = compose_operation_snapshot(repo_root=str(p), cli_overrides=overrides)
reconc_snap = compose_operation_snapshot(repo_root=str(p), cli_overrides=overrides)
Only the CLI branch (line 84-90) drives a real entry point (`from rebar._cli import main`); MCP and reconciler are re-invocations of the same function with the same arguments.
advisory.finding: The AC1 cross-surface equivalence test issues three IDENTICAL calls to compose_operation_snapshot(repo_root=str(p), cli_overrides=overrides) and labels them 'Python', 'MCP', and 'reconciler' surfaces, then asserts they are equal. This verifies the composer is deterministic, not that the MCP tool adapters or the reconciler entry point actually route through the seam with the correct mapped inputs. An adapter that mapped its inputs into cli_overrides/repo_root incorrectly would not be caught by this test — regression blindness for the AC1 claim.
scenarios: An MCP write tool or the reconciler passes the wrong repo_root/cli_overrides into emit_shadow_snapshot; the 'equivalence' test stays green because it never invokes those adapters.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that injects a fault into emit_shadow_snapshot at the reconciler entry point and asserts main() completes its authoritative pass unaffected.
evidence:
try:
 from rebar._operation_config import emit_shadow_snapshot
 emit_shadow_snapshot(repo_root=repo_root, surface="reconciler")
except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — the compatibility boundary must never break on shadow
 pass
search for `_emit_operation_shadow` in tests returned no matches — only the src definition/call site.
advisory.finding: The reconciler compatibility-boundary contract — _emit_operation_shadow swallows ALL exceptions (including an ImportError from `from rebar._operation_config import emit_shadow_snapshot`) so a shadow fault can never break reconciliation — is untested. The only fault-injection test (test_shadow_failure_does_not_break_authoritative_cli_operation) exercises the CLI surface, not the reconciler's own bare-except swallow.
scenarios: A shadow import or composition fault at the reconciler entry point; the swallow must keep the reconcile pass running, but no test proves the reconciler's own guard actually holds.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Normalize tuple leaves to lists (or document that from_document is only exact for in-process documents) so canonical_document/from_document round-trips are equal.
evidence: _validate_jsonish admits tuples: `if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):`
compose_operation_snapshot: `values = dataclasses.asdict(config)` — tuple fields stay tuples
_config_schema.py:407 `auth_jwt_algorithms: tuple[str, ...] = ("RS256", "ES256")`
_plain() copies dicts but does not normalize tuple leaves to lists, so canonical_document() carries tuples; a JSON-deserialized doc carries lists
dropped.finding: Config sections expose tuple[str, ...] fields (e.g. mcp.auth_jwt_algorithms defaults ('RS256','ES256')); dataclasses.asdict preserves these as tuples, which _validate_jsonish admits, but a canonical_document round-tripped through JSON (json.loads) yields lists, so from_document(...) rebuilt from deserialized JSON will not compare equal to the originally-built snapshot even though the documented contract presents from_document as the inverse of canonical_document.
scenarios: Any consumer that serializes a snapshot to JSON, reloads it, and calls from_document, then compares to/hashes against a freshly built snapshot
dropped.suggested_fix: Normalize sequence leaves to list in _plain() (and/or _validate_jsonish output) so both build-time and JSON-deserialized documents present lists.

search for `caplog` in tests/unit/test_operation_snapshot.py returned (no matches); the only redaction assertions (surfaces test lines 184-186) run on the WARNING path after monkeypatching fingerprint to raise.
dropped.finding: No test asserts the SUCCESS-path shadow DEBUG diagnostic honors its documented redaction contract (envelope version, source kinds, truncated fingerprint only — never config values, secrets, or file paths). The only redaction assertion is on the error/WARNING path (after a fingerprint boom), which emits a different, minimal message; the per-operation DEBUG line emitted on every successful shadow composition is never captured/asserted.
scenarios: A future edit adds a value or repo_root to the DEBUG log line; the redaction contract silently regresses because no test captures the success-path emission.
